result.topic_en: Euler eliminates the distance v to express V in terms of S and the angle Φ, then specializes the equations of motion of a flexible thread to infinitely small vibrations of a perfectly flexible string, obtaining the two equations relating tension T to the accelerations.
result.transcription:
CORP. SIVE FLEXIBIL. SEV ELASTIC. 411
constabunt, atque adeo figura totius fili ad quoduis tempus, hincque etiam ipse motus eius patefiet.

XLI. Ex tertia et quarta aequatione eliminando distantiam $v$ statim colligimus:
$$V = S\left(\frac{dd\Phi}{ds^2}\right) + \frac{dS}{ds}\left(\frac{d\Phi}{ds}\right),$$
ita vt hoc valore substituto, iam tantum duas aequationes simus habituri ex quibus si vis T elidatur statim obtinetur illa aequatio finalis principalis, cuius rationem modo explicauimus.

XLII. Quoniam praeter oscillationes infinite paruas vix quicquam adhuc circa huiusmodi motus est inuestigatum, neque etiam nunc Methodus patet tales formulas non parum intricatas tractandi, hinc saltem eas deducamus formulas ex quibus Geometrae motum cordatum vibrantium determinauerunt. Primo igitur filum perfecte flexile statuatur, vnde statim fit $V = 0$, deinde etiam vires elementares P et Q euanescant, postmodum quia tantum vibrationes infinite paruae sunt considerandae, statuamus applicatam $y$ veluti infinite paruam prae $s$ et $x$, vnde etiam erit $\frac{dy}{ds} = 0$, et $\frac{dx}{ds} = 1$; tum vero erit $\Phi$ quasi rectus. Quibus notatis nostrae duae aequationes erunt:
$$\text{I}^{\circ}.\ \left(\frac{dT}{ds}\right) = \frac{\Sigma}{2g}\left(\frac{ddx}{dt^2}\right)\sin.\Phi + \frac{\Sigma}{2g}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right)\cos.\Phi,$$
$$\text{II}^{\circ}.\ +T\left(\frac{d\Phi}{ds}\right) = \frac{\Sigma}{2g}\left(\frac{ddx}{dt^2}\right)\cos.\Phi - \frac{\Sigma}{2g}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right)\sin.\Phi.$$
Fff 2 Ra-

items.quote:
Ex tertia et quarta aequatione eliminando distantiam $v$ statim colligimus:
$$V = S\left(\frac{dd\Phi}{ds^2}\right) + \frac{dS}{ds}\left(\frac{d\Phi}{ds}\right),$$
items.english: By eliminating the distance v from the third and fourth equations we immediately obtain V = S(d²Φ/ds²) + (dS/ds)(dΦ/ds).

items.quote: Quoniam praeter oscillationes infinite paruas vix quicquam adhuc circa huiusmodi motus est inuestigatum, neque etiam nunc Methodus patet tales formulas non parum intricatas tractandi
items.english: Since, apart from infinitely small oscillations, hardly anything has yet been investigated about motions of this kind, and no method is yet available for handling such rather intricate formulas.

items.quote: hinc saltem eas deducamus formulas ex quibus Geometrae motum cordatum vibrantium determinauerunt.
items.english: Hence let us at least derive those formulas from which geometers have determined the motion of vibrating strings.
